Log Calculator

Evaluate log base b of a positive number x, answering the question b raised to what power gives x. The base is checked against the logarithm’s domain, and the change-of-base relation is shown for verification. log_b(x)=ln(x)/ln(b), requiring x>0, b>0, and b≠1. The logarithm is the inverse of exponentiation: its answer y must satisfy b^y=x. The change-of-base relation permits any valid base to be evaluated with natural logarithms.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How log is calculated

log_b(x)=ln(x)/ln(b), requiring x>0, b>0, and b≠1. The logarithm is the inverse of exponentiation: its answer y must satisfy b^y=x. The change-of-base relation permits any valid base to be evaluated with natural logarithms. log₂(32)=5 because 2⁵=32.

log_b(x)=ln(x)/ln(b), where x>0, b>0, b≠1.
A worked example

log₂(32)=5 because 2⁵=32.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Can the base be 1?

No; powers of 1 never distinguish positive inputs.

Can the input be zero or negative?

Real logarithms are defined only for positive arguments.
